BOOK: "How to Win Friends and Influence People" by Dale Carnegie
CHAPTER 35: "They Mean So Much to a Woman"
EXAMPLE: "Mayaan's Postmortem on the Forgotten Anniversary"
TONE: competitive (edge-seeking, strategic, advantage-focused)
CATEGORY: personal

CURRENT SCENARIO (lacks quoted dialogue):
Mayaan forgot Adele's birthday. First time in six years. Not malice, stress, sleep deprivation, and a calendar reminder she had turned off a year earlier because she trusted her memory. Adele said nothing for two days. That silence was the scoreboard. Mayaan traced the decline: surprise dinners in year one, calendar alerts by year four, forgotten birthday by year six. Six years of erosion compressed into one data point. The warm tone of their early relationship now exists only in Mayaan's memory, not in their present.

RULES:
- Rewrite to include at least 3 back-and-forth quoted speech exchanges using "double quotes"
- Keep the same characters, setting, and lesson
- Total length: 80-150 words
- Include 3+ concrete details (names, times, objects, locations) and 1 sensory/emotional detail
- Do NOT use em dashes (—) or double hyphens (--)
- Do NOT use banned phrases: delve, crucial, landscape, realm, furthermore, moreover
- Maintain the competitive tone
- Return ONLY the rewritten scenario text, no commentary

BOOK: "How to Win Friends and Influence People" by Dale Carnegie
CHAPTER 37: "Don't Be a "Marriage Illiterate""
EXAMPLE: "Naomi and Rhea Talk Through What They Have Been Avoiding"
TONE: gentle (warm, reflective, sit-with-it framing)
CATEGORY: work

CURRENT SCENARIO (lacks quoted dialogue):
Break room. Coffee machine clicking. Rhea and Naomi, reflecting after a workshop where three participants independently raised questions about physical intimacy in relationships.

Rhea: 'Three participants. One workshop. They are asking for content we do not offer.'
Naomi: 'I know.'
Rhea: 'We keep stepping around this because David thinks it is too sensitive. But the participants are already bringing it up on their own.'
Naomi: 'I have been avoiding the conversation. You are right.'
Rhea: 'What if we frame it as a credibility gap rather than a content addition? David listens when credibility is on the line.'
Naomi: 'Pull the participant feedback. I will get us on his calendar Thursday.'
